title: Mia login & consent: choose the layout
question: Your brand colours and type stay fixed. Pick the layout for the sign-in, sign-up and consent flow. All three are fully responsive.

options.label: Conversational concierge
options.thesis: Mia asks one short question at a time, and your answers stack up like a quiet boutique conversation.
materials: answered steps collapse into editable chips
options.viewport: A sheet with 'Hi, what's your mobile number?' in serif, one field and one pink CTA. Earlier answers sit above it as tappable chips.
options.risk: The profile and consent step has a lot of copy, which can break the one-question rhythm and feel slow on desktop.

regions.label: Mia asks: What should we call you?

options.label: Stepped side drawer
options.thesis: A right-hand drawer on desktop and a full-height sheet on mobile, with a thin progress rail and one clear task per step. Preferences gets its own final step.
options.viewport: The page stays visible behind a 440px drawer. The rail reads Mobile, Verify, Details, Preferences. The CTA is pinned to the bottom so the keyboard never hides it.
options.risk: Four visible steps make sign-up look longer than it is. Returning users only see two of them.

options.label: Compact typographic card
options.thesis: A small centred card with no photo. Serif title, generous white space, and consent in the details step as a tidy expandable group.
materials: OTP fills inline in the same card
options.viewport: A white card centred on a soft grey veil showing the logo, 'Sign in or sign up', the phone field and a pink Send OTP button. The card resizes smoothly between steps.
options.risk: Without the promo image the ₹500 offer has less pull. It needs a small offer ribbon to keep it.
